scenes.narration: In the summer of fifteen eighteen, a woman stepped into a street in Strasbourg and started to dance.
Her name was Frau Troffea. There was no music, and she did not stop.
She danced for almost a week. Then her neighbors began to join her.
Within a month, around four hundred people were dancing in the streets, unable to stop.
City leaders had a strange idea. They thought the cure was more dancing.
So they built a stage, hired musicians, and paid strong men to keep the dancers moving.
It made things worse. Exhausted dancers collapsed, and some reportedly never got up.
Historians still argue about the cause. Mass stress, famine and fear are the leading theories.
Others blame ergot, a mold on rye bread that can cause spasms and hallucinations.
Whatever it was, the dancing plague remains one of history's strangest mysteries. What do you think caused it?
